summary: MySQL is writing fast statements into the slow query log because `log_queries_not_using_indexes=ON` expands logging beyond the `long_query_time=2` threshold.
symptoms: Slow-log lines show `Query_time` values around 0.0003 to 0.0023 seconds, far below the configured 2-second threshold.
The same log lines show `Rows_examined` values in the hundreds to low thousands.
The user expected only slow queries in the slow log but observed many fast statements there.
mechanism: With `slow_query_log=ON`, MySQL logs statements that exceed `long_query_time` and also logs statements that do not use indexes when `log_queries_not_using_indexes=ON`. That means a fast full scan on an unindexed predicate can appear in the slow log even when it is nowhere near the time threshold.
